subject: CardinalPay Redwood integration — implementation transfer and connector checklist
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cardinalpay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Kapoor <samir@payflux.io>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood integration — next steps and requirements

Hi Olga / Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We're ready to move to an implementation kickoff but need a clear handoff doc and an explicit checklist for the connector (SDK bootstrapping, endpoint migration, retry windows, rate fences). Attached is our integration requirements spreadsheet (high level).

High level asks from our side:
- Minimal downtime for our endpoint migration window (target maintenance window Oct 20–21)
- Guidance for SDK usage in Node + Go (auth, streaming responses)
- Recommended retry/backoff & a recommended per-client rate limit profile (we have spikes up to 120 RPS for batch jobs)
- Any suggested canary strategy and rollback checklist (we require audit logs for each rollout)

Can you put together a concise implementation transfer that we can share with our platform team? We'd like the CSM/implementation owners mapped out so we can schedule the kickoff.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
VP, Platform Engineering — CardinalPay

Attachment: cardinalpay-impl-requirements.xlsx

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cardinalpay.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood integration — next steps and requirements

Hi Elaine — thanks for the spreadsheet, this is perfect. I've sketched a short implementation transfer below and attached the MVP cookbook and connector samples. Proposed owners:

- CSM & kickoff: Olga Petrov (implementation lead) — schedule + mutual action plan
- SDK & sample code: Ben Carter (developer liaison) — Node/Go examples, timeout defaults
- Routing / rate fences: Kimberly Park (platform ops) — rate profile & canary routing policy

Implementation transfer (summary):
1) Pre-kickoff (by Oct 13)
   - Confirm maintenance window and DNS failover plan (Elaine + Ops)
   - Share exact peak RPS traces for top 3 endpoints (CardinalPay)
2) Sandbox build (Oct 14–18)
   - Team pulls connector-samples.tar.gz, uses sample SDK init below to validate auth and streaming
   - Validate token rotation path and KMS integration for production keys
3) Canary (Oct 20)
   - 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% in 30–60 minute increments with automatic fallback to hosted variant on error >=5% over baseline errors
4) Cutover (Oct 21)
   - Full routing shift with rollback plan and post-cut metrics check (latency, 95/99 p50)

Minimum recommended SDK snippets (Node & Go) — put these in our samples repo; Ben will expand:

Node (example):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, host: 'https://api.redwood.ai' });

// streaming example w/ timeout and retry wrapper
await client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: '...' }, { timeoutMs: 120000 });

// recommended HTTP timeout: 60s default, 120s for long streams

Go (example):
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("RW_API_KEY"))
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, redwood.GenerateParams{Model: "redwood-small", Prompt: "..."})

Retries: use exponential backoff with jitter (base 200ms, max 8s, max attempts 5). For streaming endpoints prefer idempotent-safe resume via KV cache prefix when possible.

I've attached: cardinalpay-mvp-cookbook.pdf, connector-samples.tar.gz, and the requirements sheet you sent.

I'll coordinate a 30-minute internal pre-kickoff with Ben and Kimberly tomorrow to triage the sample code and rate profile. Proposed kickoff: Oct 14 at 10am PT — does that work for your team?

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: cardinalpay-mvp-cookbook.pdf, connector-samples.tar.gz

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: FW: CardinalPay Redwood integration — implementation transfer (action items)

Team — forwarding Elaine's asks and the transfer summary. Quick alignment notes and owners below (action items are short):

Action items:
- Ben (owner): expand Node + Go samples (auth rotation, streaming resume, short circuit for partial responses). Build a sample that simulates a 5% error injection so we can demo fallback. Deliverable: sample repo + README by Oct 12.
- Kimberly (owner): propose a per-client rate profile that fits CardinalPay spikes (suggested plan: 100 RPS baseline, burst bucket to 200 for 10s with token bucket enforcement). Also prepare routing policy: canary weights + automated fallback to hosted variant. Deliverable: policy draft by Oct 12.
- Olga (owner): coordinate sandbox credentials and host the pre-kickoff sync (Oct 8 internal).

Notes on reliability and retries (internal defaults we should push in samples):
- Default request timeout: 60s; streaming timeout: 120s
- Retry strategy: only retry on 5xx or network errors; do NOT retry on 4xx except 429 with a backoff suggested header read
- Backoff: exponential jitter (attempts=5, base=200ms, cap=8000ms)
- Token-level throttling: recommend tagging high-volume clients and applying a per-token per-second quota at the edge; instrument counters for spike windows to adjust quickly.

Please reply with any blockers. Ben — can you include a short snippet that shows the backoff wrapper and how to surface retry metrics to our tracing?

Olga
